html:
SMTO-WEB-0029 — The answer didn't use the sources or number of results you asked for

GUID: 8ee2a3e6-78a4-5cbd-8ecd-912b32297037
Slug: research-required-source-missing
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web_research

What happened

  • Your request asked for particular sources or a certain number of results, and the answer doesn't meet that yet. SMTO won't present it as complete.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the run to finish. SMTO sends the answer back to the Model and asks it to use the sources you required and reach the number of results you asked for. The check compares the answer with the sources and result count in your request.
  2. If the run stops, check your request: if you named specific websites or excluded some, make sure those are what you want. SMTO only accepts sources your request allows, and never sources you told it to avoid.
  3. If fewer results are acceptable, tell SMTO it may give a partial answer that says how many it could confirm. A partial answer with a clear note about what's missing is allowed.

What success looks like

  • The answer uses the sources you asked for and the number of results you wanted, or clearly says what's still missing.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't accept an answer that counts unconfirmed results toward the number you asked for.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Research proof found unmet source requirements: required observation URLs not observed, fewer verified results than minimum_results, or a claim citing supplementary or forbidden sources the contract disallows.

What this means

  • Proof lacks required observations or minimum verified results, or a claim uses supplementary or forbidden sources outside the contract. This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.

Why this can happen

  • Proof lacks required observations or minimum verified results, or a claim uses supplementary or forbidden sources outside the contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect missing observation URLs, allowed source rules and the verified-result count.

How to fix it

  • Raised as research_required_source_missing in _validate_answer (rejection details carry missing_observation_count, claim_id or 'Requested result count not met'). Observe the required URLs, cite only permitted, non-forbidden sources, reach minimum_results, or complete with status partial and the [[research_summary]] limitation.
  • Use permitted evidence and fulfill the specific source or result-count requirement, or report what remains unverified.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use verified facts or an explicit scoped limitation.

How to verify the fix

  • The answer meets those source/count requirements or states a validated partial limitation.

What not to do

  • Do not claim the required sources or result count were satisfied by unverified candidates.

Technical notes

  • This is an opt-in research proof check. With enforcement disabled the runtime retains the answer; observation mode can record a fault without blocking it. Rejected proof does not erase completed source access or authorize another acquisition.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
